newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN LINEAR BONDS SEEN HEADING UP AFTER PAUSE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN LINEAR BONDS SEEN HEADING UP AFTER PAUSE.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds, which outperformed Bunds on Wednesday as light profittaking pared strong gains in late trading, are expected to resume their seemingly inexorable climb after the pause, traders said.
"This market is very strong. Perhaps we are a bit euphoric and may come down again in a couple of weeks, but for now we are going up," one trader said.

Such was the strength of the Belgian market that the spread of 10-year bonds over German Bunds fell to a record low of seven basis points just before the close, with some traders said to be aiming at a narrowing to just five basis points.
"I personally don't think it will get there, but in this market it doesn't take much to get movement," one trader said.
Traders said the market had been fairly quiet throughout the day, with the focus of attention on 10-year paper and some earlier maturities.
"The very long end was very disappointing," one trader remarked.
Traders made no mention of Thursday's Bundesbank Council meeting that is expected to maintain the status quo on interest rates.
The benchmark 2006 OLO ended yielding 6.05 percent against Tuesday's closing 6.09 percent. The spread over Bunds was eight basis points against 12.
The december futures contract was 29 basis points up at 119.65 near the middle of a 119.82/119.43 range.
